question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Buy a lemon

options.text: To buy something that is of much less value.
To work through the day and shop in the evening
To give importance to little things

solution:
The correct answer is **'To buy something that is of much less value'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Buy a lemon" **is used when someone purchases something (typically a vehicle or any mechanical device) that is found to be defective or less satisfactory than expected.
 
• So, the most appropriate meaning is *"To buy something that is of much less value".*

Therefore, the **correct answer **is:* 'To buy something that is of much less value.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the meanings of the other options:
 
 
• **"To lose foundation" **refers to losing the basic structure or underlying basis of something.(आधार खो देना)
 
• **"To work through the day and shop in the evening"** is a literal phrase describing a person's daily routine.(दिनभर काम करना और शाम में खरीदारी करना)
 
• **"To give importance to little things" **means to pay attention to or value the small details or aspects of life or a situation.(छोटी चीजों को महत्व देना)
 
 

3a:T618,

The correct answer is 'Option 4'.
